cases.name: curvature.minkowski_pipeline_ok
cases.reference: compute_curvature accepts a genuinely static metric

cases.name: curvature.minkowski_christoffel_zero
cases.notes: constant field, so the stencil sums to exactly zero -- this is an exactness claim, not a tolerance
cases.reference: Gamma^rho_{mu nu} = 0 for a constant metric

cases.name: curvature.minkowski_riemann_zero
cases.notes: passes trivially for a pipeline that always returns zero; curvature.flat_spherical_riemann_zero is the case that does not
cases.reference: R^rho_{sigma mu nu} = 0 in flat Cartesian coordinates

cases.name: curvature.flat_spherical_connection_nonzero
cases.notes: separates a vanishing connection from vanishing curvature
cases.reference: Gamma != 0 although the spacetime is flat

cases.name: curvature.flat_spherical_christoffel_closed_form
cases.notes: interior only; boundary worst = 0.001061 (one-sided stencils, reported separately by policy)
cases.reference: Gamma^r_{th th} = -r, Gamma^th_{r th} = 1/r, Gamma^ph_{th ph} = cot(th), ...

cases.name: curvature.flat_spherical_christoffel_closed_form_boundary
cases.notes: a one-sided second-order stencil has a larger error constant; reported and bounded separately rather than averaged into the interior figure
cases.reference: same, on the one-sided shell

cases.name: curvature.flat_spherical_riemann_zero
cases.notes: the case a sign error in the Gamma-Gamma terms fails; boundary worst = 0.062516
cases.reference: R^rho_{sigma mu nu} = 0 for flat space in ANY chart

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_pipeline_ok
cases.reference: the time-dependent path produces a result

cases.name: curvature.christoffel_lower_pair_symmetry
cases.notes: algebraic in the assembly, so this is roundoff and not truncation
cases.reference: Gamma^rho_{mu nu} = Gamma^rho_{nu mu} (torsion free)

cases.name: curvature.metric_compatibility
cases.notes: does NOT reuse the Christoffel formula, so it is an independent identity; exact to roundoff because the same discrete d_alpha g enters both sides. boundary worst = 0.000000
cases.reference: nabla_lambda g_{mu nu} = 0 for the Levi-Civita connection

cases.name: curvature.riemann_antisymmetry_last_pair
cases.notes: manifest in the assembly; roundoff, not truncation
cases.reference: R^rho_{sigma mu nu} = -R^rho_{sigma nu mu}

cases.name: curvature.riemann_first_bianchi
cases.notes: holds algebraically for any symmetric connection, so it tests the index wiring rather than the discretisation
cases.reference: R^rho_{[sigma mu nu]} = 0

cases.name: curvature.riemann_antisymmetry_first_pair
cases.notes: O(h^2), not roundoff -- see the product-rule note above. Boundary worst = 0.002268. curvature.convergence_ricci_symmetry demonstrates the order
cases.reference: R_{rho sigma mu nu} = -R_{sigma rho mu nu} (indices lowered)

cases.name: curvature.riemann_pair_exchange
cases.notes: O(h^2); boundary worst = 0.001448
cases.reference: R_{rho sigma mu nu} = R_{mu nu rho sigma}

cases.name: curvature.ricci_symmetry
cases.notes: O(h^2); boundary worst = 0.001542. A5 forms G_{mu nu} = R_{mu nu} - (1/2) g_{mu nu} R and will inherit exactly this asymmetry, so the size of it is a number that milestone needs
cases.reference: R_{mu nu} = R_{nu mu}

cases.name: curvature.schwarzschild_ricci_flat
cases.notes: boundary worst = 0.062684
cases.reference: R_{mu nu} = 0 (vacuum Einstein equation)

cases.name: curvature.schwarzschild_ricci_scalar_zero
cases.notes: boundary worst = 0.007825

cases.name: curvature.schwarzschild_kretschmann
cases.notes: relative error, interior only; boundary worst = 0.161128. Ricci flat but NOT flat -- the case that separates the two
cases.reference: R_{abcd} R^{abcd} = 48 M^2 / r^6

cases.name: curvature.chart_connections_differ
cases.notes: max|g_schw - g_iso| = 0.053344, confined to the radial component for the reason above. Without this the invariance case below could be comparing a chart with itself
cases.reference: the two charts describe the same geometry with different Gamma^rho_{mu nu}

cases.name: curvature.kretschmann_chart_independent
cases.notes: exact value 48/5^6 = 0.003072; isotropic midpoint rho = 3.936492 is the exact root of rho + M + M^2/(4 rho) = 5
cases.reference: K is a scalar: its value at areal radius 5 does not depend on the chart

cases.name: curvature.kretschmann_isotropic_closed_form
cases.reference: K(rho) = 48 M^2 / r(rho)^6 in isotropic coordinates

cases.name: curvature.desitter_ricci_scalar
cases.notes: relative; exact value 3.000000. Maximally symmetric, so a radial trend in the error is unambiguously discretisation. boundary worst = 0.164122
cases.reference: R = 12/L^2 for de Sitter, everywhere

cases.name: curvature.desitter_ricci_scalar_sign
cases.notes: a pipeline with the opposite Riemann sign returns -12/L^2 and passes every identity check in this suite; this is the case that catches it
cases.reference: R > 0 for de Sitter under the MTW (+,+,+) conventions of docs/conventions.md section 6

cases.name: curvature.desitter_ricci_proportional_to_metric
cases.notes: absolute, against components of size 0.75 to 1.7; measured 2.0e-2 on this grid. Componentwise, not merely the trace; boundary worst = 0.065779
cases.reference: R_{mu nu} = (3/L^2) g_{mu nu}

cases.name: curvature.desitter_kretschmann
cases.notes: relative; measured 1.07e-2 on this grid; exact value 1.500000
cases.reference: R_{abcd} R^{abcd} = 24/L^4

cases.name: curvature.desitter_ricci_square
cases.notes: relative; exact value 2.250000
cases.reference: R_{mu nu} R^{mu nu} = 36/L^4

cases.computed_description: temporal policy is Refused: TimeTreatment::FrozenTimeDiagnostic discards d_0 g -- curvature built from a discarded temporal derivative is not the curvature of any spacetime
cases.name: curvature.frozen_time_refused
cases.notes: docs/conventions.md section 11 requires refusal rather than a warning: imposing d_0 g = 0 on a metric that depends on t gives an inconsistent input to the Christoffel formula, not the curvature of some other static spacetime
cases.reference: a Refused temporal policy yields no curvature at all

cases.computed_description: ExactlyStatic was claimed (Alcubierre (a deliberately false claim) has no t dependence in this chart; d_0 g vanishes identically rather than being discarded) but the metric changed by 0.119730 between t and t+h
cases.name: curvature.false_static_claim_refused
cases.notes: probe residual = 0.119730. Without this, a moving bubble declared static would be frozen silently -- the failure the refusal above exists to prevent, arriving through a different door
cases.reference: ExactlyStatic is verified against the sampled metric before use

cases.name: curvature.rigid_translation_identity
cases.notes: roundoff, not truncation: with h_t = h_x/v_s the temporal taps land on the same u values the spatial stencil uses. x-boundary worst = 0.006270 (one-sided in x, centred in t, so O(h^2) there by construction)
cases.reference: d_0 g = -v_s d_x g exactly, for x_s(t) = v_s t

cases.name: curvature.frozen_time_would_be_materially_wrong
cases.notes: the refusal is not pedantry; this is the size of the error it prevents
cases.reference: discarding d_0 g changes the Ricci scalar by an amount comparable to the Ricci scalar itself

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_zero_velocity_flat
cases.notes: v f = 0 for every f, so the metric is constant and the stencils sum to exactly zero -- an exactness claim
cases.reference: v_s = 0 gives g = eta exactly, hence R^rho_{sigma mu nu} = 0

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_reference_point_on_grid
cases.notes: no interpolation enters the comparison
cases.reference: every reference coordinate is an exact grid coordinate

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_ricci_scalar_vs_symbolic
cases.notes: worst at (2.000000,0.000000,0.000000); the reference uses EXACT metric derivatives and independently written algebra, so the gap is this pipeline's O(h^2) truncation error and is expected to fall fourfold per refinement
cases.reference: R against exact symbolic differentiation of the closed form

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_ricci_tensor_vs_symbolic
cases.notes: componentwise, not merely the trace
cases.reference: R_{mu nu} componentwise against the symbolic reference

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_kretschmann_vs_symbolic
cases.reference: R_{abcd} R^{abcd} against the symbolic reference

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_ricci_square_vs_symbolic
cases.reference: R_{mu nu} R^{mu nu} against the symbolic reference

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_centre_finite
cases.notes: the shape function is even in r_s so d_x f = f'(r_s) x/r_s is a removable 0/0 there. The symbolic reference cannot evaluate it and excludes the point; the grid pipeline never forms the ratio, so it can and does
cases.reference: curvature is finite at r_s = 0

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_axial_symmetry
cases.notes: the y and z grids are identical, so this is exact to roundoff and detects any asymmetry introduced by the index wiring
cases.reference: R(x,y,z) = R(x,z,y): the bubble is axisymmetric about x

cases.name: curvature.alcubierre_asymptotically_flat
cases.notes: structural, not a closed form
cases.reference: curvature at the far corner is small compared with the wall

cases.name: curvature.convergence_schwarzschild_kretschmann
cases.notes: orders: 9->17 = 1.936604, 17->33 = 1.984386. The finest pair is the one asserted; the coarse pair is recorded because a coarse grid is not yet in the asymptotic regime
cases.parameters: M=1, evaluated at the pinned midpoint r=5
cases.reference: K error falls as O(h^2) under refinement

cases.name: curvature.convergence_flat_spherical_riemann
cases.reference: the spurious Riemann of flat space falls as O(h^2)

cases.name: curvature.convergence_ricci_symmetry
cases.notes: order 17->25 = 2.124725. R_{mu nu} is symmetric in the continuum; the residual is a property of the discretisation and must vanish with it
cases.reference: the Ricci antisymmetry induced by the discrete product rule falls as O(h^2)

cases.name: curvature.convergence_alcubierre_ricci_scalar
cases.notes: order 9->17 = 1.351316. Demonstrating the order here is what makes the fixed-tolerance comparison in the alcubierre group a check rather than a calibration
cases.reference: R converges to the symbolic reference at O(h^2), including the resampled temporal derivative

title: Covariant curvature: Christoffel symbols, Riemann and Ricci tensors, curvature invariants, and the temporal-derivative policy they require
